candidate.label: Deterministic expected-TTR D fit
candidate.construct: D parameter fitted to a sample-size/TTR curve

definition.probability_evaluation: group types by increasing integer frequency; for each frequency compute the absent probability by multiplying ((N-f-i)/(N-i)) for i=0,...,n-1 in increasing order; accumulate spectrum_count*(1-absent) in increasing frequency order
definition.objective: unweighted sum over requested sample sizes of (g(n,D)-y_n)^2
optimizer: for each 0<y_n<1 compute D_n = n*y_n*y_n/(2*(1-y_n)) in the written operation order
bracket log(D) by log(min(D_n)) and log(max(D_n))
bisect the analytic derivative with respect to log(D) exactly 100 times
iterate sample sizes in increasing order and accumulate terms left to right
a zero derivative moves the upper bound, selecting the smaller D in a tie
definition.legacy_variant: vocd_d_mc_python_v0 uses Python random.Random/random.sample, sizes 35:50, 100 trials, three seeds, and a censored grid; it is a distinct historical compatibility method
definition.identity_limit: this is a D-curve fit to an exact finite-population hypergeometric expected-TTR curve; it is neither CLAN VOCD nor claimed to be the infinite-repetition limit of CLAN output
definition.validation_tolerance: absolute 1e-12 plus relative 1e-12 for binary64 reference values

computational_domain.condition: N >= max(requested sample_sizes), all requested expected TTR values are in (0,1), and the finite stationary solution is unique

either a single-crossing proof for every admissible frequency spectrum or a deterministic global-minimum fallback with an explicit smaller-D tie rule
a preregistered construct-redundancy and admission analysis relative to HD-D, MATTR, and MTLD, including length and near-hapax strata
machine-readable Windows UCRT x86-64, Linux x86-64, and macOS arm64 results
